extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys, and patent examiners (KIPO) dealing with divisional and converted applications in Korea
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules for filing, examining, and determining effects of divisional and converted (utility model→patent) applications under the Korean Patent Act and its Enforcement Rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amend parent application to differentiate claims when filing a divisional
rubrics_metrics.description: When filing a divisional application the applicant is supposed to amend the parent application to differentiate the invention(s) claimed in the parent from the claims of the divisional application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parent need not be amended where the inventions claimed in the divisional are disclosed only in the description of the invention or drawings of the parent application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and documents for disclosure-exception / priority claims in a divisional
rubrics_metrics.description: If a claim for disclosure exception or a priority claim is to be made for a divisional application, the applicant shall state the purport of the claim and submit the evidential documents by the prescribed date from the filing date of the divisional application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prescribed times: within 30 days from filing for disclosure-exception claims; within 3 months for priority claims. If such claims were not made at the time of filing the parent, they are not recognized at the time of filing the divisional, except limited exceptions when purport was set in the parent but evidential documents were not timely submitted — those can be submitted within the divisional's prescribed period (unless the parent claim was invalidated before divisional filing).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliance on evidential documents of the parent application
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may rely on evidential documents already submitted for the parent application when filing a divisional if the evidential documents for both are identical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant may substitute submission for the divisional by stating the purport of using the parent's evidential documents in the attached form documents. Where documents were submitted at the parent's filing and the same claim appears in the divisional, it is deemed the applicant intended to refer to the parent's documents — but Article 10(2) Enforcement Rules requires the intention to be stated. If intention not stated and documents not submitted, examiner shall request amendment citing violation of description formalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisional generally retains parent's filing date, with exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: A divisional application shall retain the same filing date as the parent application unless particular conditions make retroactive filing-date benefit unfair.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of when divisional shall be deemed filed on its actual filing date: (①) divisional corresponds to 'another application' under Article 29(3) of the Patent Act or to a 'patent application' under Article 4(3) of the Utility Model Act; (②) where applicant requests application of proviso of Article 30(1)(1) and certain evidential filings; (③) where priority under Treaty is claimed but purport/country/date requirements not met; (④) where domestic priority is claimed but prior-filed application not properly indicated. New subject matter added to divisional specification/drawings should not get parent's filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formality and eligibility checks on filing a divisional
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon submission of a divisional, the examiner shall first check whether the application fulfills the formality requirements for a divisional and whether the filer is eligible, the filing is within the designated period, and the parent application is properly stated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If filed by a person not eligible to divide, filed after designated period, or filed after termination of parent pendency, examiner shall give opportunity to explain; failure to explain within designated period leads to returning the written divisional application (citing Article 11(1)(7) or (11)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of permissible amendments to a divisional while pending
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments to a divisional application are allowed while the divisional is pending but only to correct obvious errors or deficiencies; amendments that change the contents (introduce new subject matter) are not accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should notify applicant of the scope allowed for amendment in an amendment request form; if divisional fulfills procedural and substantive requirements it will be treated as a regular application and amendment permissibility assessed accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination of divisional scope depends on filing-date regime (pre-/post-2006)
rubrics_metrics.description: The substantive examination standard for a divisional depends on whether the parent was filed before Sept 30, 2006 or on/after Oct 1, 2006, especially when the divisional claims inventions not described in the parent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If parent pre-2006 and divisional claims inventions not described in parent, examiner issues preliminary notice for inadmissible division and, if division not accepted, examines on divisional's actual filing date; the published parent gazette can be used as prior art. If parent on/after Oct 1, 2006, examiner shall notify grounds for rejection and decide to reject if not cured by argument/amendment. If inventions not described are deleted by amendment, examiner may examine based on the parent's filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of parent published gazette as prior art when retroactivity denied
rubrics_metrics.description: When a divisional cannot take the parent's filing date and is examined on its actual filing date, the published patent gazette of the parent can be cited as prior art to deny novelty or inventive step.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner may issue notice for inadmissible division and proceed to examine on the divisional's actual filing date; when both inadmissible division and rejection grounds exist, examiner should confirm acceptance status before issuing rejection notice, but may issue both notices in separate forms when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deletion of non-disclosed inventions by amendment can restore parent's filing date
rubrics_metrics.description: If inventions not described in the parent are deleted through amendment of the divisional's specification/drawings while examining (even when retroactive filing date was not initially allowed), the examiner shall examine the divisional based on the filing date of the parent application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This allows restoration of the parent's filing date for the divisional where impermissible subject matter has been removed during examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisional may claim Treaty or Domestic priority; reference dates determined by earliest relevant filings
rubrics_metrics.description: A divisional application may claim priority under the Treaty or Domestic Priority; reference date(s) for patentability of each invention are determined by the filing date of the prior-filed application that first disclosed the given invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When chains of filings exist, the divisional retains the filing date of its immediate parent for subject matter covered by that parent's filing, but the reference date for a specific invention may be an earlier prior-filed application depending on which application first disclosed that invention. See provided example (Inventions B, C, D). Article 36(2) applies when same invention described in both.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisional cannot be based on multiple parent applications
rubrics_metrics.description: A divisional application shall not be filed based on multiple parent applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exception: a divisional can be filed based on a parent application that itself claims domestic priorities from two or more prior-filed applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special treatment when parent received decision to grant on/after 29 July 2015
rubrics_metrics.description: When examining a divisional from a parent that received a certified copy of decision to grant on or after July 29, 2015, examiners must take account of conflicts and pending correction trials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant does not request trial for correction when filing a divisional for an invention disclosed only in parent description or recited in the parent's claims, examiners should check whether claimed inventions are identical and inform applicant of conflicting application in the rejection notice. If applicant divides a portion of an invention described in the granted parent with a trial for correction requested, examination of the divisional should be deferred until the trial concludes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion eligibility: utility model → patent conversion within disclosure scope
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant who filed a utility model registration application may convert it into a patent application within the scope of the disclosure in the original specification or drawings, subject to statutory exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conversion is not allowed in certain cases (e.g., more than 30 days have passed since first certified copy of a decision to reject was served; the utility model application was filed in a foreign language and required Korean translation was not submitted upon filing the converted application).

rubrics_metrics.name: Converted application generally retains original filing date, with enumerated exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: A converted application is deemed filed at the time the utility model application was filed, except where application of that filing date would be unfair under specified statutory provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions include cases where Article 29(3) of the Patent Act or Article 4(4) of the Utility Model Act applies, Article 30(2) applies, Article 54(3) applies, or Article 55(2) applies (i.e., similar fairness/other-application situations as for division).

rubrics_metrics.name: Must state intention and identify original application when filing conversion
rubrics_metrics.description: A person who intends to file a converted application must state his/her intention and indicate the utility model application to be converted in the patent application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the original application is not stated or is incorrectly stated at filing, conversion will not be deemed legitimate. Amendments correcting the indication of the original application are not accepted except for explicit errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of filing a converted application: original utility model deemed withdrawn
rubrics_metrics.description: When a converted application is filed, the corresponding utility model registration application shall be deemed withdrawn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After the original is deemed withdrawn due to conversion, the original will not be valid even if the converted application is later invalidated, withdrawn, abandoned, or finally rejected — except where the converted application is returned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and documents for disclosure-exception / priority claims in a converted application
rubrics_metrics.description: If claiming disclosure exceptions or priority for a converted application, the applicant must describe the purport of such claims in the converted application and submit the necessary evidential documents within the prescribed period from the filing date of the converted application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prescribed times: 30 days from filing for disclosure-exception; 3 months for priority. Claims not made at the time of filing the original application are generally not accepted (with specified exceptions for applications filed on/after 29 July 2015). If the purpose was described in the original but evidential docs were not submitted, submission until the converted's prescribed date can render the claim legitimate unless the original procedure had been invalidated before conversion. Applicant may rely on already-submitted evidential documents of the original application by stating the purport of reliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Converted application must be pending at KIPO at time of conversion
rubrics_metrics.description: To be recognized as legitimate, the utility model registration application before conversion must be pending before KIPO at the time of conversion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A converted application shall not be filed when the original application has been invalidated, withdrawn, abandoned, or registered. If filed on the same date the original procedure terminated due to withdrawal/abandonment, the converted application is deemed filed when the original was pending.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive requirement for converted application: within original disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: A converted application is legitimate only if the matters disclosed in the converted application's specification/drawings are included in the original application's specification/drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If even a single matter disclosed in the converted application is not contained in the original, the converted application is illegitimate and subject to rejection. Determination uses criteria of explicit description or whether the invention is understood to be disclosed without explicit wording (see 'Scope of Amendment' reference).

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for filing a converted application (Form and statements required)
rubrics_metrics.description: When filing a converted application the applicant must file a new patent application attaching the specification or relevant documents (Form XIV) and state the purport of the converted application and identify the original application forming the basis of conversion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to properly state the original application or incorrect indication will render conversion not legitimate. Reliance on evidential documents of the original can be stated instead of resubmission where identical. Specific additional procedural rules apply for foreign-language filings (translations), claim insertion when original lacked claims, and fees/translations for international applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination formality checks and opportunity to explain for converted applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon submission of a converted application the examiner shall check formality requirements, eligibility of filer, whether conversion was within allowed period, and whether the original application is properly stated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the converted application appears filed by an ineligible person, after the allowed period, or after termination of original procedure, examiner shall give opportunity to explain; failure to explain within the designated period results in returning the converted application (citing Article 11(1)(7) or (11)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination regimes for converted applications based on original filing date (pre‑1999 and post‑2006)
rubrics_metrics.description: Examination of converted applications is categorized by the time the original application was filed; if the converted claims inventions not described in the original, examiner actions vary by regime.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If original filed before July 1, 1999: issue preliminary notice for inadmissible conversion and, if not accepted, examine on actual filing date and may cite original gazette as prior art; deletion by amendment of non-disclosed inventions allows examination based on original filing date. If original filed on/after Oct 1, 2006: notify grounds for rejection and decide to reject if not cured by arguments or amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment periods and new matter prohibition for converted applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments to the specification/drawings of a converted application are allowed only within the period prescribed in Article 47(1), retroactively counted from the filing date of the original application; new subject matter added after filing is prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If converted fulfills procedural and substantive requirements, it is treated as an ordinary application and examined for amendment permissibility using the original specification/drawings. The prohibition also applies where an invention described in the original application but not in the converted's original attachments is later attempted to be added.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on combining division and conversion in a single procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: A converted application may be filed taking a divisional as the original application, but division and conversion carried out in a single patent procedure (e.g., converting part of a patent application to a utility model within same procedure) renders conversion illegitimate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant intends to change types, they should file a divisional first and then file a converted application based on that divisional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling conversion when filing with reexamination or appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: When an applicant files a converted application while requesting reexamination or appealing a rejection of the original application, the examiner shall accept the converted application if the procedure is legitimate in formalities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon request for examination of the converted application, the examiner conducts examination while treating the original application as deemed withdrawn per Article 53(4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification when converted application cannot take original filing date (EDMS use)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a converted application cannot retain the filing date of the original (e.g., original was returned after conversion), the examiner shall examine the converted application based on the actual filing date and shall notify the applicant (using the On-nara/EDMS system) why the converted application cannot take the retroactive filing date along with grounds for rejection if any.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In absence of rejection grounds, examiner still must notify the applicant why retroactive filing date cannot be given.
